about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Rajma Chawal Punjabi Kidney Beans with Rice
recipes.summary: Soft kidney beans in a thick onion and tomato gravy, pressure-cooked and served over rice.

items: 300g dried kidney beans, soaked overnight and drained

steps: Boil the soaked beans hard in fresh water for 10 minutes to destroy the natural toxins, drain, then pressure-cook in the 4 cups water with 1 tsp salt for 25 minutes at high pressure until completely soft, then release the pressure.
Fry the onions in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, then add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in the turmeric, cumin and tomatoes and cook 8 minutes until the oil separates.
Tip in the beans with their liquid, add the garam masala and simmer 10 minutes until the gravy is thick.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes, and serve with the beans.

recipes.title: Sambar Rice Plate Tamil Lentil and Vegetable Stew
recipes.summary: A tamarind-sour lentil stew with drumstick-style vegetables, pressure-cooked and eaten over rice.
steps: Pressure-cook the lentils with the water and turmeric for 12 minutes at high pressure until they are completely soft, then release the pressure and mash lightly.
Add the onion, carrots, eggplant, tomatoes, tamarind and curry powder and simmer for 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds until they crackle and stir into the pot.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Serve the sambar over the rice.

recipes.title: Bisi Bele Bath Karnataka Spiced Lentil Rice
recipes.summary: A one-pot hot lentil rice with vegetables, tamarind and a roasted spice blend, finished with ghee.
steps: Pressure-cook the lentils, rice and water with the turmeric for 15 minutes at high pressure until completely soft and mushy.
Release the pressure and stir in the vegetables, tamarind, spice mix and 1 tsp salt.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the vegetables are soft and the mixture is thick like porridge, adding hot water if too stiff.
Heat the ghee, pop the mustard seeds until they crackle and pour over the top.

recipes.title: Thukpa Gyathuk Tibetan Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.summary: A comforting Tibetan noodle soup with chicken, vegetables and ginger.
steps: Fry the onion, ginger and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the chicken and cook 4 minutes, then pour in the water, soy sauce and pepper.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C, adding the carrots for the last 8 minutes.
Add the noodles and bok choy and cook 4 minutes until tender.
Ladle into bowls and top with spring onions.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C in the centre. Contains gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Shapta Tibetan Stir-Fried Beef with Capsicum
recipes.summary: Quick stir-fried beef with onion, capsicum and chilli, served with rice.
steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Sear the beef in 1 tbsp hot oil for 3 minutes in two batches until browned, then set aside.
Fry the onion, capsicums, garlic, ginger and chillies in the remaining oil for 5 minutes.
Return the beef, add the soy sauce and peppercorns and toss for 2 minutes until the beef reaches 71°C.
Spoon the beef and vegetables over the rice and serve straight away while the capsicum is still crisp.
notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Chicken Haleem Pakistani Slow-Cooked Wheat and Lentil Stew
recipes.summary: A thick, spiced porridge-like stew of chicken, wheat and lentils, topped with ginger and fried onion.
steps: Rinse the wheat and lentils, then pressure-cook with the water, turmeric and 1 tsp salt for 30 minutes at high pressure until completely soft.
Fry one onion in 2 tbsp oil until golden, add the ginger, garlic and chicken and cook 8 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir the chicken mix and spices into the cooked wheat, simmer 20 minutes and beat with a wooden spoon until thick and smooth.
Fry the second onion in the remaining oil for 10 minutes until crisp.
Serve topped with fried onion, ginger and lemon.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C in the centre. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Karahi Gosht Peshawari Lamb
recipes.summary: A simple Peshawari lamb karahi with tomato, ginger and black pepper, no onion, eaten with flatbread.
steps: Heat the ghee in a karahi or heavy pan and sear the lamb in batches for 8 minutes until browned.
Add the garlic and half the ginger and fry 2 minutes, then the tomatoes, chillies, pepper, cumin and 1 tsp salt.
Cover and cook on low for 35 minutes until the lamb is tender and reaches 71°C and the oil separates.
Stir in the coriander and the remaining ginger and serve with the flatbreads.
notes: Food safety: cook the lamb to at least 71°C. Contains milk and gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Plov Uzbek Carrot and Beef Rice
recipes.summary: The festive Uzbek rice pilaf of beef, carrot and chickpeas cooked under a lid.

items: 1 whole garlic bulb, top sliced off

steps: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot and brown the beef for 8 minutes, then add the onions and cook 8 minutes until golden.
Add the carrots and cumin and fry 6 minutes, then pour in half the water and 1 tsp salt and simmer, covered, for 30 minutes until the beef is tender and reaches 71°C.
Rinse the rice, spread over the meat, add the chickpeas, remaining water and garlic bulb pressed into the centre.
Cover and cook on low for 20 minutes until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed.
Rest 10 minutes, then mix gently and serve.
notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Lagman Uzbek Beef and Vegetable Noodle Stew
recipes.summary: Hand-pulled style noodles under a thick beef, capsicum and tomato stew.
steps: Brown the beef in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the onions and cook 5 minutes.
Add the carrots, capsicums, garlic, tomato paste and cumin and cook 4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and water and simmer for 30 minutes until the beef is tender and reaches 71°C.
Boil the noodles until tender, about 4 minutes, and drain.
Serve the stew over the noodles.
notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Contains gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Dal Tadka Pressure-Cooker Yellow Lentils with Tempering
recipes.summary: Creamy yellow lentils finished with a sizzling garlic, cumin and chilli tempering.
steps: Pressure-cook the lentils with the water, turmeric, tomato and 1 tsp salt for 12 minutes at high pressure until completely soft, then release the pressure and whisk smooth.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat the ghee, fry the cumin seeds until they crackle, then add the onion and cook 5 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and chillies for 1 minute and pour the sizzling mix over the dal.
Scatter with coriander and serve with the rice.

recipes.title: Anda Curry Spiced Egg Curry
recipes.summary: Boiled eggs in a thick onion and tomato gravy with garam masala.
steps: Hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool and peel, then score lightly.
Fry the onions in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, then add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in the spices and tomatoes and cook 8 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the water and simmer 5 minutes, slide in the eggs and warm 3 minutes.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes, and serve with the curry.
notes: Food safety: hard-boil the eggs until the yolk is firm. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Bhuna Khichuri Bengali Roasted Lentil Rice
recipes.summary: A rainy-day Bengali rice and lentil dish with vegetables and ghee, pressure-cooked.
steps: Dry-roast the lentils in a pot for 4 minutes until fragrant and light golden.
Melt the ghee, fry the cumin and bay leaves until the seeds crackle, then add the ginger and turmeric.
Add the rice, lentils, vegetables, water and 1 tsp salt and pressure-cook for 10 minutes at high pressure until soft.
Release the pressure, stir well and serve thick and porridge-like.

recipes.title: Nihari Pakistani Slow-Braised Beef Shank
recipes.summary: A rich, silky beef braise in a gingery spiced gravy, traditional for festive breakfasts and Eid.
steps: Fry the onions in the ghee for 15 minutes until deep brown.
Add the beef, grated ginger, garlic and spices and brown for 8 minutes.
Pour in the water, bring to a simmer and cook, covered, for 2 hours until the meat is falling apart and reaches 71°C.
Stir the flour with 1/2 cup water until smooth, add to the pot and simmer 10 minutes until the gravy is glossy.
Serve topped with ginger matchsticks and lemon.
notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Contains milk and gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Aloo Gosht Pakistani Lamb and Potato Curry
recipes.summary: Everyday lamb and potato curry, pressure-cooked until tender.
steps: Fry the onions in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, then add the garlic and ginger.
Add the lamb and spices and brown for 6 minutes, then stir in the tomatoes.
Add the water and pressure-cook for 20 minutes at high pressure until the lamb is tender and reaches 71°C.
Release the pressure, add the potatoes and simmer 12 minutes until tender.
Serve with the flatbreads.
notes: Food safety: cook the lamb to at least 71°C. Contains gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Kofta Challow Afghan Meatballs with Rice
recipes.summary: Spiced beef meatballs in a tomato sauce over fragrant rice.
steps: Mix the beef, grated onion, spices, coriander and egg with 1 tsp salt and roll into 16 balls.
Fry the chopped onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the tomatoes and paste and cook 6 minutes.
Add the water, bring to a simmer and add the meatballs, cooking gently for 20 minutes until the meatballs reach 75°C inside.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Serve the meatballs and sauce over the rice.
notes: Food safety: cook the meatballs to 75°C in the centre. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Borani Banjan Afghan Eggplant with Garlic Yoghurt
recipes.summary: Fried eggplant in a tomato sauce, topped with garlic yoghurt and dried mint, served with flatbread.
steps: Brush the eggplant slices with 3 tbsp oil and roast at 220°C for 25 minutes until soft and golden.
Fry the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, add the turmeric and tomatoes and cook 12 minutes until jammy.
Layer the eggplant in a dish, spoon the tomato sauce over and simmer 5 minutes.
Mix the yoghurt with the garlic and a pinch of salt, spoon over the top and dust with mint.
Serve warm with the flatbreads.

recipes.title: Sabzi Challow Afghan Spinach and Lamb
recipes.summary: A slow-cooked spinach and lamb stew, deeply green, served with rice.
steps: Brown the lamb in the oil for 8 minutes, add the onion and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, coriander, turmeric and water, cover and simmer for 30 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Stir in the spinach in handfuls and cook 10 minutes until the stew is thick and the lamb reaches 71°C.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Finish the stew with lemon juice and serve over the rice.
notes: Food safety: cook the lamb to at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Shurpa Uzbek Lamb and Vegetable Soup
recipes.summary: A clear, hearty lamb soup with big chunks of potato, carrot and tomato.

items: 700g lamb shoulder, cut into large pieces

steps: Simmer the lamb in the water with the onions and 1 tsp salt for 45 minutes, skimming, until nearly tender.
Add the carrots and potatoes and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, capsicums and cumin and simmer 8 minutes until all the vegetables are tender and the lamb reaches 71°C.
Stir through the dill and serve in large bowls.
notes: Food safety: cook the lamb to at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Dimlama Uzbek Layered Lamb and Vegetable Pot
recipes.summary: A layered pot of lamb, potato, carrot and cabbage steamed in its own juices with no stirring.
steps: Layer the onions, then the lamb, cumin and 2 tsp salt, in a heavy lidded pot brushed with oil.
Layer in the potatoes, carrots, cabbage, tomatoes and garlic, drizzle with oil and add the water.
Cover tightly and cook on very low heat for 90 minutes without stirring until the lamb is tender and reaches 71°C.
Rest 10 minutes and serve straight from the pot.
notes: Food safety: cook the lamb to at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Sekuwa Nepali Grilled Chicken Thigh Skewers
recipes.summary: Spice-rubbed chicken grilled until charred, served with rice and sliced onion.

items: 800g chicken thigh fillets, cut into chunks

steps: Mix the chicken with the yoghurt, ginger, garlic, spices, oil and 1 tsp salt.
Thread onto metal skewers and grill or barbecue over a high heat for 14 minutes, turning, until charred and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Serve the sekuwa with rice, onion and lemon.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C in the centre. Contains milk. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Thenthuk Tibetan Hand-Torn Noodle Soup with Beef
recipes.summary: Torn dough noodles in a spiced beef and vegetable broth.
steps: Knead the flour with the 150ml water and 1/2 tsp salt into a firm dough and rest 20 minutes under a damp cloth.
Fry the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 5 minutes, add the beef and cook 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, soy sauce and 5 cups water and simmer 12 minutes until the beef reaches 71°C.
Flatten and tear the dough into thin pieces, drop them in and cook 5 minutes until tender, adding the spinach for the last minute.
notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Contains gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Shapaley Tibetan Beef Pasties
recipes.summary: Crisp half-moon pastries filled with spiced minced beef and onion.
steps: Knead the flour, water and 1/2 tsp salt into a smooth dough and rest 20 minutes under a damp cloth.
Mix the beef, onion, garlic, ginger, pepper and soy sauce into a filling.
Roll the dough thin, cut into 10cm rounds, fill each, fold over and crimp the edges.
Fry in oil heated to 170°C for 3 minutes per side until deep golden and the filling reaches 75°C.
Drain on paper and serve hot.
notes: Food safety: cook the beef filling to 75°C in the centre. Contains gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
